cells.tense: A build is on its last step and you are holding it there while it finishes.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Give an afternoon to picturing what follows a piece of work that's done, then take the first small step toward it.
cells.core: You keep a thing going past the interesting part, when others have drifted off, and that is a real skill. Keeping it also means setting down what's done. An ending here isn't a wall, it's a door, and your even hand is what gets people across the sill. The whole build is close, and something in you can already picture the next plot of ground. That picture is yours, but it only becomes real if you move toward it. So give an afternoon to imagining what follows — what it looks like, who's in it — and take the first small step that way. The hard part is already behind you. The next step is lighter because your own hand is the one pointing at it.
cells.sheetLine: What you kept going is done, so walk through the open door.
cells.verb: tending the fire under something so it can finish and open into the next
cells.place: the step where a build is finally whole and only now gives way to what comes next

cells.tense: Where a thing is meant to be finished, you will be pushing it past its own edge.
cells.act: say the hard thing gently, once
cells.ask: Say one true thing plainly to someone you're holding up, without softening it, and tend nothing after it for a week.
cells.core: You keep momentum alive in the ones near you, and that has earned trust. When it runs hot, holding someone up turns into pushing: you can feel a thing near its end and add fuel anyway, because watching it sit finished feels like dropping it. So the person who needs a plain word from you keeps getting hints instead. You're bracing at a future you can't write by force. The outcome sits behind a door they have to open, and fuel won't open it for them. Say one hard thing once — gently, plainly — and then nothing. If this read is wrong and nobody was braced, no damage is done: they heard something true from someone who carries weight. The quiet you're dodging is smaller than the collapse you're racing.

cells.tense: Where a thing could be finished, it stays open behind you while the fire runs low.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Hold one lingering thing untouched for three days, then finish it for good in a single clear evening.
cells.core: Somewhere in you the one who keeps the fire going hasn't shown up in a while, and whatever that's about belongs to your life, not to this draw. What's visible is the build stuck on its last step, something left open that could have closed, and the fuel it takes to stand in that doorway. Nobody can order you to want it again. What's left is smaller than wanting. Hold one lingering thing untouched for three days, then finish it in a single clear evening. The things you hold onto sit better when the ones you're through with are gone. That's the whole ask for now. If it turns out to be the wrong room, you've cleared an evening and found out which one is right.

cells.tense: You are carrying changes through to the end and telling the room you're undecided.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Move one piece of a change you've already settled on — an email, a shelf, a bag heading out the door — and don't announce it as a decision.
cells.core: Finished things near you cross the line while you describe yourself as someone who hasn't chosen. Someone has to steady the middle of a project, hold the plan when others change course, take the keys at the end — that work is happening through you, and it doesn't make the cut of the story you tell about yourself. The story says drifting. The ones moving alongside you say something else. So here's the ask, small and plain: move one piece of a change you've already made up your mind about. One shelf cleared, one bag carried out, one message sent. It doesn't need to be announced. If the read misses, you've improved one shelf and seen who was standing close. The shift was yours. Letting it be named yours can come later, and in the simplest shape first.

attempts.check: The draft claims the person knows what is finished and still keeps feeding it — the record supports a build that will not integrate or release, not foresight about their own endings; a reader could rightly say nothing here says what they know or don't. The diagonal ask survives being wrong: telling one hard thing plainly costs little even where the bracing was never about a kept thing. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'you know exactly which piece is finished' — cut it; several cells lean on a kept piece I inferred, so every keeping clause should read as one instance they can refuse, and the balance's cost stays concrete (a piece stays in and others keep their footing once it goes).
